title: Pulaski County mother mourning after 7-year-old is killed in accidental home shooting - NewsBreak
text:
By Mike Rogers ,
4 hours ago
PULASKI COUNTY, Ark. — A Pulaski County mother is sharing her heartbreak after her 7-year-old son was shot and killed in what investigators say was an accidental shooting involving a loaded firearm left unattended inside a home.
According to the Pulaski County Sheriff’s Office, deputies responded just after 6 p.m. Tuesday to a home along Highway 107 after receiving a report that a child had been shot. When deputies arrived, they found 7-year-old Everett Deaver suffering from a gunshot wound to the stomach, according to his mother.
Jacksonville North Pulaski School District releases statement after 7-year-old killed in shooting Investigators say another child inside the home found a loaded revolver that had been left unattended. Authorities allege 31-year-old Michael Deaver had the firearm inside the home after returning from work before going outside to speak with a neighbor. The younger child, 4 years of age, then gained access to the gun and accidentally shot Everett.
Everett was rushed from the scene by ambulance before being flown to Arkansas Children’s Hospital. His mother, Sydni McGraw, said she learned about the shooting while she was at her home in Cave City.
“I wasn’t there,” McGraw said. “My husband had gotten a call while I was in the shower that Independence County was looking for me. I called them back and they said that my baby had been shot.”
McGraw and her husband immediately drove toward Little Rock, while her parents headed to the hospital ahead of them.
“My daddy called me and told me that my baby was gone,” she said.
Despite the devastating loss, McGraw said she does not want anger to define her son’s memory.
“From what I understand, Michael had gotten home from work and was unloading his stuff and put the firearm on the counter,” she said. “The firearm shouldn’t have been left out, but I want to make one thing clear — I’m not mad at the daddy. It was a crazy accident.”
Instead, she hopes Everett’s death serves as a reminder for gun owners to securely store their firearms.
“If you have that firearm on the counter and you don’t think your child can reach it, think a second,” McGraw said. “Just lock your guns up before you get home.”
A neighbor who witnessed the emergency response described the frantic moments as first responders worked to save Everett’s life.
“I heard the sirens and as they got closer they just stopped, so I thought, ‘That must be close,’” the neighbor said. “When I came outside there were police everywhere and an ambulance. They were wheeling the little boy out on a gurney, and you could tell they were moving pretty quick.”
The neighbor said he had often seen Everett playing outside.
“I’ve watched him play. Just a good kid,” he said. “From what I could tell, he was just your average kid. It’s tragic for a 7-year-old’s life to be cut short.”
7-year-old shot and killed by another child with unattended gun in Pulaski County, 1 arrested He also echoed McGraw’s message about firearm safety, saying parents should not only securely store guns but also educate children about them.
“If you’re going to have them around, you’ve got to teach them about them,” he said. “You never know what friend your kid’s going to bring home.”
Following the investigation, the Pulaski County Sheriff’s Office arrested Michael Deaver. He was charged with manslaughter and three counts of first-degree endangering the welfare of a minor.
The investigation remains ongoing.
For McGraw, the hope is that no other family experiences the pain she now carries.
“He just had so much life and love in his little body,” she said.
